platform: Mac and Windows beta. Linux, iPhone and Android are planned.
pricing: Vendor says it is free. Invite-only beta; purchases made through the assistant still cost money, and Underdog says it earns a small share of those purchases.
cons: Invite-only beta.
description: A private assistant that runs on your computer for email, calendar, meeting notes, dictation and errands.

name: Fo by Wajo
platform: Its pages describe text, phone, email and Slack; the exact messaging apps were not verified.
pricing: Fo Mini is free with a daily limit. OG Fo is free once unlocked by invite. Pro is by contacting the company.
pros: Free tiers available.
cons: Free use has a daily limit. Pro has no public price.
description: An assistant for calls, email, tasks and bookings, with a human fallback.

name: Skye
platform: iPhone and iPad app; requires iOS/iPadOS 26.0 or later.
pricing: Its terms say certain features are currently free; paid plans may be introduced with 30 days notice.
pros: Vendor says it surfaces what matters on the home screen.
cons: Requires iOS/iPadOS 26.0 or later.
description: A personal AI home-screen app with cards, widgets, chat and daily briefings based on your context.

name: Stanley
platform: iMessage, Telegram, WhatsApp and web.
pros: Made for one specific creator workflow.
description: An agent for creators and content work, not general personal errands. Its pages disagree on where it works: some list iMessage, Telegram and web, while the live welcome page offers Telegram and WhatsApp. An older Stanley iPhone app (Instagram coaching, by FindCommunity, Inc.) is still on the App Store; Stanley says it has upgraded the product, and we have not tested whether the old app still works. The old app is not the current agent, and its pricing does not apply. Stan also lists a separate Stanley app for drafting LinkedIn posts. We have not tested how it connects to this messaging agent.

name: Town
platform: Web and iPhone app (needs iOS 26.0 or later), plus texting (iMessage, RCS or SMS) and assistant chat on Telegram or WhatsApp.
pricing: Free: 30 chats/month. Starter $15/month billed monthly with 1,250 credits (usage units). Pro $59/month, Power $119/month and Power Plus $239/month billed monthly, or the equivalent of $49/$99/$199 per month billed annually, with 5,000/12,000/40,000 monthly credits. Pay-as-you-go on Pro and above is off until you raise the $0 spending cap.
pros: Individual plans plus separate team plans.
description: A work-first assistant for individuals. It works in a chat; it cannot read your other WhatsApp chats, but it can work in connected email and Slack.
